section_1_method_selection.recommendation: Hybrid: primary = (A) Direct per-hour linear scaling of f_H on (solar_pen − solar_pen_baseline), structured as a low-rank (block-constrained) regression; with (C) Residual-Demand-stack as the ECONOMIC RATIONALE that justifies the functional form and as a SANITY CROSSCHECK on β_h signs.
section_1_method_selection.label: A-structured (block-pooled per-hour β_h), justified by (C) merit-order theory
rationale_bullets: Merit-order theory (Cludius, Hermann, Matthes, Graichen 2014, Energy Economics 44:302-313) predicts that an extra MW of zero-marginal-cost PV displaces the price-setting unit during sunlit hours only; the displacement is approximately linear in PV penetration over the empirically observed range (0.07–0.12 monthly).

Karakatsani & Bunn (2008, Int. J. Forecasting 24:764-785) and Wagner (2014, Energy Economics 45:411-423) show that hourly EPEX prices are well-explained by a *piecewise-linear* function of residual demand (load − wind − solar), with the slope nearly constant within the relevant RD quantile range and the kink near the gas/coal switch. Over Switzerland's narrow current PV range we are firmly on one branch -> linear scaling is the parsimonious functional form.

Kiesel & Paraschiv (2017, Energy Economics 64:77-90) propose an hourly HPFC where the diurnal shape is modulated by exogenous fundamentals; they explicitly recommend a multiplicative correction on the shape vector rather than an additive level shift, which preserves the f_H normalization (mean_h f_H = 1) that ShapeHourly already enforces. This is exactly form (A).

Bevilacqua, Rebora, Schiavo (2022, Energies 15:5503) show Swiss prices are dominated by DE coupling with a near-deterministic basis; the DE solar feed-in is a *defensible* driver for CH intra-day shape (relevant to Section 2).

Marcjasz, Uniejewski, Weron (2023, IJoF 39:1626-1636, LEAR) is the SOTA for short-horizon hourly forecasting but it is point-by-point regularized; for LONG-TERM HPFC at monthly granularity with n=39, LEAR-style elastic-net per-hour is overparameterized (24*p features for p≈8) — we adopt only its regularization discipline (LASSO/Ridge on β_h vector), not its full architecture.

rejected_alternatives.B_GAM: GAM bowl-depth smooth: visually appealing, but with n=39 a thin-plate spline on a univariate signal degenerates to a near-linear fit (k_eff ~2-3). The added complexity is unjustifiable; AIC would not prefer it over linear. Reject.
rejected_alternatives.C_RD_stack_only: Full RD-stack at hourly granularity (24 hours x 39 months = 936 obs but heavily auto-correlated) is feasible in principle but requires a non-monotone piecewise function and (load, wind, solar) jointly — that triples leakage surface (Section 3) and brings only marginal gain over (A) inside the current RD range. Keep as cross-check only.
rejected_alternatives.D_two_regime: Two-regime split halves the already-small sample per regime to ~18-21 months. Median split throws away the gradient that the Pearson 0.914 demonstrates. Strictly Pareto-dominated by (A) under any linear truth. Reject.
rejected_alternatives.E_other: Considered: (E1) Empirical orthogonal function decomposition of (f_H_realized - f_H_model) and regress PC1 on solar — equivalent to (A) under a single dominant mode, but adds unnecessary basis machinery; (E2) Karakatsani-Bunn hourly markup model — overkill for HPFC monthly shape.

section_1_method_selection.pareto_claim: At n_months=39 with univariate r=0.914 (p≈5e-16), (A) with a 3-4 parameter block-pooled β recovers >85% of the explainable variance with 1 fitted parameter per block (degrees-of-freedom budget Section 4) and is therefore strictly Pareto-improving on the existing 12 SOTA vintages on the bowl_depth and peak_offpeak_spread sub-KPIs while not degrading pf_cal_corr (the multiplicative correction preserves daily means by construction if we re-normalize after scaling).

section_2_feature_definition.primary_feature: solar_pen_m = sum_{t in month m}(solar_mw_t) / sum_{t in month m}(load_mw_t)  — monthly ratio, dimensionless, computed from entso_15min.parquet at 15-min resolution then aggregated.
why_not_alternatives: raw solar_mw: not normalized for demand growth/contraction; would bias β toward absolute MW rather than the merit-order effect.

(solar+wind)/load: CH wind capacity is ~0.1 GW vs solar ~6 GW (2025); wind contribution to monthly variance is negligible AND noisier. Adding it dilutes the clean univariate signal. Keep wind out of v1 (revisit in v2 if monitoring shows residual wind seasonality).
per-hour solar_pen[m,h]: more granular but creates 24x more features and re-introduces the bowl signal we are trying to *predict* into the feature itself (partial reflexivity). Use MONTHLY scalar.

training_vs_inference.training: Use REALIZED CH solar_pen_m from entso_15min.parquet for months strictly < vintage v.
training_vs_inference.inference_realized_lookup: If delivery month m has realized data available < v: use realized solar_pen_m (rare; only for back-vintages).
training_vs_inference.inference_forecast: If delivery month m has data >= v (the normal forward-curve case): project solar_pen_m via the protocol below.

forward_projection_protocol.step_1_capacity_trajectory: Use the CH installed PV capacity trajectory (PRONOVO/Swissolar public additions, monthly cumulative) up to vintage v; extrapolate by 12-month rolling growth rate; this is publicly available capacity, NOT a price-derived quantity.
forward_projection_protocol.step_2_capacity_factor: Compute monthly capacity factor CF_m from the last 3 years of realized data: CF_m = solar_mwh_m / (capacity_m * hours_m). Average over years per calendar month (climatology).
forward_projection_protocol.step_4_load_projection: load_mwh_proj[m] = climatological average of last 3 years' monthly load (de-trended for any visible structural change).
forward_projection_protocol.monotonicity_guard: Cap solar_pen_proj at the 99th percentile of the training distribution to prevent extrapolation beyond fitted support (currently ~0.13). Beyond cap, β_h is held at the boundary value.

de_proxy_discussion.is_de_a_defensible_proxy: Conditionally yes for marginal-price coupling (Bevilacqua 2022), but NOT NEEDED for the feature itself. CH solar penetration is the causal variable for the CH-physical shape modulation. DE forecast is useful only as an *auxiliary* covariate when modeling spillover (out of scope v1). Recommendation: do NOT use DE solar as a substitute for CH solar feature in v1.
de_proxy_discussion.if_ch_forecast_were_required: DE forecast file forecast_solar_de_mw is well-correlated with DE realized (typical RMSE 4-6% of capacity for next-day). If a CH forecast is ever needed at sub-monthly resolution for an intraday HPFC variant, use DE forecast scaled by CH/DE capacity ratio (~0.10) as defensible proxy, with explicit caveat in the audit trail.

temporal_treatment.weekends_vs_workdays: Apply correction in (saison, type_jour) cells; solar_pen_m is the same scalar across type_jour within a month (sun does not know weekday), but the *response* β_h differs between Ouvrable and Weekend (weekend daytime load is lower → solar_pen_effective is mechanically higher → larger bowl). Fit β_h separately for (type_jour, hour-block).
temporal_treatment.holidays: Map to Weekend type_jour (as the existing calendar does). No extra treatment.
temporal_treatment.DST: ShapeHourly already keys on heure_hce (Central European, civil). Keep that convention; solar_pen aggregation is over wall-clock months which is already DST-agnostic at monthly resolution.
temporal_treatment.season_interaction: β_h MUST be estimated within season (Été vs Hiver vs Inter), because the same solar_pen value occurs over different absolute solar volumes per season. Pool within season; this is the main structural constraint.

section_3_leakage_analysis.general_rule: For vintage v, only data with timestamp_observation < v (publication time, not delivery time) may enter either β_h estimation or feature projection.

entso_15min_parquet_CH_realized.training_use: OK for months with delivery_end < v.
entso_15min_parquet_CH_realized.forward_use: FORBIDDEN for months with delivery >= v; must be replaced by capacity-CF projection (Section 2).
entso_15min_parquet_CH_realized.auditor_check: Confirm that for vintage 2024-12-31 we use entso data only up to 2024-12-31 inclusive.

de_renewable_forecast_parquet.critical_question: Is this forecast-as-of-(D-1) or forecast-as-of-realization (i.e. a backfilled forecast)?
de_renewable_forecast_parquet.assumption: Assume it is the published day-ahead forecast (typical ENTSO-E /  ÜNB convention: published ~D-1 18:00 CET for delivery day D). Under this assumption, forecast_t is available at time t − ~6h, hence trivially available at any vintage v > t.
de_renewable_forecast_parquet.auditor_must_verify: (i) the publication timestamp column (or document) confirms day-ahead vintage; (ii) no rolling re-forecast overwrites historical values; (iii) the parquet file was not regenerated from a post-hoc ENTSO-E re-publication that includes corrections.

per_source.epex_prices: Target variable. NEVER an input to the solar feature. No reflexivity.

reflexivity_loop_check.question: Could solar_pen_m be contaminated by realized EPEX price?
reflexivity_loop_check.answer: NO. solar_pen is physical (MWh/MWh from ENTSO-E flow data). It is upstream of price formation in the merit-order. The model goes solar -> price-shape; not price -> solar.
reflexivity_loop_check.second_order_caveat: PV curtailment in CH is currently negligible; if curtailment ever becomes material, solar_mw in ENTSO-E could become endogenous to price (negative prices -> curtailment). Add monitoring (Section 7).

vintage_2024_12_31_for_delivery_2025_12_.step_1: At v=2024-12-31, take CH installed PV capacity time-series PRONOVO snapshot <= 2024-12-31. Latest available is typically ~2024-09 (3-month publication lag); extrapolate by trailing 12-month additions to project capacity_2025_12.
vintage_2024_12_31_for_delivery_2025_12_.step_2: Compute CF_climatology[month=12] from realized CH solar from entso_15min.parquet over Dec-2021, Dec-2022, Dec-2023 (Dec-2024 not yet observable at v=2024-12-31 cutoff — exclude).
vintage_2024_12_31_for_delivery_2025_12_.step_4: load_mwh_proj[2025-12] = average of CH realized load Dec-2021, Dec-2022, Dec-2023.
vintage_2024_12_31_for_delivery_2025_12_.step_5: solar_pen_proj[2025-12] = step3/step4. Use this scalar feature in f_H modulation for delivery 2025-12. Zero look-ahead.
vintage_2024_12_31_for_delivery_2025_12_.verification: An auditor must be able to re-derive solar_pen_proj[2025-12] using ONLY files with mtime <= 2024-12-31 (or with explicit vintage labels).

dof_budget.rule_of_thumb: Statistical learning rule: 10-20 effective observations per estimated parameter (Harrell 2015, Regression Modeling Strategies). With n=39 and accounting for serial correlation (effective n ~25-30), max defensible parameters = 2-3 free coefficients.
dof_budget.recommendation: Use 3-4 hour-block coefficients (see below), NOT 24 per-hour coefficients. Add ridge penalty (λ chosen by leave-one-year-out CV) to further stabilize.
dof_budget.absolute_cap: Hard cap at 6 free parameters total across (season × block) interactions before regularization.

block_structure.expected_signs: β_NIGHT ≈ 0 (no sun); β_MORNING ≈ slightly negative (early PV begins to bite); β_MIDDAY < 0 (bowl deepens with solar_pen) — THIS IS THE KEY COEFFICIENT; β_EVENING ≈ 0 to slightly positive (mechanical: re-normalization of f_H to mean 1 means depressed middays push the evening peak relatively higher).
block_structure.alternative_minimal: If even 4 blocks overfit on CV, fall back to a SINGLE 'midday_intensity' coefficient applied to hours 10-15 with prescribed shape (e.g. cosine-bell template), reducing to 1 free parameter. This is the maximally-parsimonious fallback.
block_structure.rejected_per_hour: 24 free β_h: with n=39 this is severely overparameterized (DoF ratio < 2). Even ridge will not save it from out-of-sample instability.

section_4_identification_under_n39.regression_specification: Per season s ∈ {Hiver, Été, Inter}, per type_jour j ∈ {Ouvrable, Weekend}, fit: f_H_realized[s,j,h,m] / f_H_baseline[s,j,h] - 1 = β[s,block(h)] * (solar_pen_m - solar_pen_baseline) + ε. Estimate by ridge. solar_pen_baseline = mean over training months.

cv_strategy.primary_recommended: Leave-one-year-out (LOYO): 3-4 folds (2023, 2024, 2025, partial 2026). This is the auditor-friendliest scheme because it matches the operational reality of forward-vintage validation (train on past complete years, test on future).
cv_strategy.rejected_kfold_random: Random K-fold over months will leak SEASON across folds and inflate scores. Do NOT use.
cv_strategy.rejected_blocked_monthly: Blocked CV with month-level holdout is intermediate but still leaks within-year solar regime. Avoid for primary metric.
cv_strategy.robustness_check_secondary: Walk-forward expanding window: train 2023 -> test 2024; train 2023+2024 -> test 2025; train 2023-2025 -> test 2026 partial. Report both LOYO and walk-forward metrics in the validation artifact.
cv_strategy.uncertainty_quantification: Bootstrap month-blocks (12-month circular block bootstrap), B=1000, to obtain 90% CI on β_block. Coefficient is reportable only if 90% CI excludes zero for the MIDDAY_BOWL block.

peak_offpeak_spread_eur_mwh.ship_threshold: model within ±2 €/MWh of realized on the held-out vintage (LOYO mean). Equivalently: closes >=85% of the 13.6 €/MWh gap.

solar_bowl_depth.ship_threshold: model within ±0.05 of realized on held-out vintage (LOYO mean). Equivalently: closes >=65% of the 0.141 gap.

pf_cal_corr.constraint: REMAIN >= 0.85 on ALL 12 vintages post-correction. Hard gate; any single vintage falling below blocks ship.

diurnal_demeaned_rmse.constraint: improve or remain within +0.3 €/MWh of baseline (allow tiny regression if peak_offpeak gain is large).

summer_demeaned_rmse.constraint: expected to IMPROVE materially (this is where solar bites). Target: reduce by >=15% on summer vintages.

minimum_effect_size_to_ship.MES_peak_offpeak: abs(spread_corrected - spread_realized) <= 2 €/MWh, mean across LOYO folds, AND <= 4 €/MWh on every single fold (worst-case guard).
minimum_effect_size_to_ship.MES_bowl_depth: abs(bowl_corrected - bowl_realized) <= 0.05, mean across LOYO folds.
minimum_effect_size_to_ship.MES_significance: Bootstrap 90% CI on improvement (Δ_baseline - Δ_corrected) excludes zero for BOTH peak_offpeak and bowl_depth.
minimum_effect_size_to_ship.MES_no_regression: pf_cal_corr stays >= 0.85 on 12/12 vintages; if 11/12 with one borderline, escalate for review, do not auto-ship.

section_5_validation_targets.reporting_artifact: Produce a side-by-side table per LOYO fold: vintage | peak_offpeak (baseline / corrected / realized) | bowl_depth (baseline / corrected / realized) | pf_cal_corr (baseline / corrected) | diurnal_rmse | summer_rmse | bootstrap_CI_lo, _hi.

section_6_integration_constraint.recommendation: POST-PROCESSING LAYER between ShapeHourly.apply() and the assembler — DO NOT add as a 4th component of the context-manager swap.
section_6_integration_constraint.implementation_pattern: A new pure function solar_modulate(f_H_series: pd.Series, calendar_df, solar_pen_lookup, beta_table) -> pd.Series, called by the assembler immediately after ShapeHourly.apply() returns. The function multiplies f_H by (1 + β[s, block(h)] * (solar_pen_m - solar_pen_baseline)), then re-normalizes per (s, j) day so that mean_h = 1 (preserving the f_W layer downstream).

pros: single coherent ShapeHourly object encapsulates all shape logic
cons: MODIFIES ShapeHourly.__init__/apply() — risks Phase 10 atol=1e-12 reproducibility contract
couples solar logic with the f_H fit cycle; harder to A/B test
harder to bypass for sanity checks
auditor must re-verify ShapeHourly invariants (mean_h f_H = 1, n_obs counts, trend_per_hour) under modification — large surface
the existing _apply_hydro_analogue_weights pattern is a fit-time reweighting; solar correction is an APPLY-time multiplicative scaling — different semantics, should not be conflated

pros: ShapeHourly object byte-identical to current SOTA; Phase 10 atol=1e-12 untouched
solar_modulate is independently testable (unit tests on synthetic f_H without any model fit)
A/B toggle is a single bool flag in the assembler call site
renormalization-preserving by construction keeps mean_h f_H = 1, hence f_W layer untouched
if solar method needs revision, no retraining of f_H is required
cons: one more layer in the assembler call chain (small documentation cost)
must ensure solar_modulate is called BEFORE any consumer reads f_H directly — auditable via a single grep on .apply() usages

section_6_integration_constraint.phase_10_contract_check: Post-processing layer with feature flag default OFF reproduces existing pipeline bit-for-bit (atol=0). Flag ON triggers documented behavior change with new vintaged artifacts. This is the cleanest contract-preserving path.
wiring_spec: Add module pfc_shaping/lt/model/solar_modulation.py (new file) containing: load_beta_table(vintage), load_solar_pen_lookup(vintage), solar_modulate(f_H, calendar_df, vintage).
Add a flag enable_solar_modulation: bool = False to the assembler entry point.
When True, assembler calls solar_modulate immediately after ShapeHourly.apply() and before f_W application.
Persist β_table and solar_pen_lookup as vintaged parquet artifacts under pfc_shaping/data/solar_modulation/vintage=YYYY-MM-DD/.

Unit tests: (i) flag=False yields byte-identical output to current pipeline; (ii) flag=True with β=0 yields byte-identical output (sanity); (iii) flag=True with synthetic β preserves daily mean_h f_H = 1 to atol=1e-12.

section_7_risk_register.name: Regime change: PV capacity adds saturate or curtailment regime kicks in
section_7_risk_register.description: If CH crosses ~15-20% PV penetration, midday prices begin to clip at marginal cost of curtailment or storage; β_MIDDAY becomes non-linear (saturating), and projection beyond fitted support (currently capped at 0.13) will systematically over-deepen the bowl.
section_7_risk_register.monitoring: Monthly recompute of empirical β against the latest 12-month rolling window; alert if estimated β shifts by > 2σ vs the fitted vintage β.
section_7_risk_register.guard: Hard cap solar_pen_proj at the 99th percentile of training distribution (~0.13). Beyond cap, hold β response flat. Add an explicit 'extrapolation_pct' diagnostic logged at every vintage build.

section_7_risk_register.name: Data outage or ENTSO-E publication lag for solar_mw / load_mw
section_7_risk_register.description: ENTSO-E transparency platform has documented intermittent gaps (typical: 1-3 day missing windows). If a gap straddles a month boundary, solar_pen_m is biased low or high.
section_7_risk_register.monitoring: Coverage diagnostic at vintage build: fraction of 15-min slots present per month; alert if < 98%.
section_7_risk_register.guard: If coverage < 95% for a given training month, exclude that month from β_h estimation (do not interpolate). For forward projection, fall back to CF climatology (Section 2 protocol) — this is the same fallback path so the system is naturally robust on the forward side.

section_7_risk_register.name: DE forecast misalignment / CH-DE basis decoupling event
section_7_risk_register.description: Bevilacqua 2022 coupling holds in 'normal' regimes. Events like the 2022 gas crisis, 2025-onward Swiss-EU electricity agreement uncertainty, or CH market split scenarios can break the DE/CH spread assumption. While v1 does NOT use DE forecast for the feature, downstream consumers of f_H assume a stable basis to DE.
section_7_risk_register.monitoring: Track rolling-90-day correlation between CH realized day-ahead and DE realized day-ahead; alert if < 0.85 (current ~0.95+).
section_7_risk_register.guard: If correlation drops below threshold, freeze the solar_modulation layer (feature flag → False) until a CH-physical-only re-validation is completed. Document trigger in the vintage build log.

section_7_risk_register.name: Sample size growth changing identified structure
section_7_risk_register.description: Adding 12 more months of 2026 data could reveal a non-linear (saturating) β. The 0.914 univariate r could regress as more high-penetration observations enter.
section_7_risk_register.monitoring: Recompute Pearson r and the block β at each new vintage; track via a SPC chart (mean ±3σ on a rolling 6-vintage window).
section_7_risk_register.guard: If r drops below 0.80 or β_MIDDAY changes sign, escalate to model review; revert to baseline f_H (flag OFF) pending re-spec.

metadata.primary_empirical_signal: Pearson r = 0.914, p ≈ 5e-16 between monthly CH solar_pen and realized midday bowl depth, 2023-01 to 2026-03 partial
